ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, managers, shareholders and material transaction counterparties against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) guidelines, CSSF lists, Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases as required by Article 3(2) of the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU autonomous sanctions lists (EU Regulation 269/2014 and all associated implementing regulations), and the Belgian-Luxembourg sanctions enforcement framework. Additionally, because the target payment rails are SWIFT wire and letters of credit, the filing banks require OFAC, EU and UN sanctions screening plus enhanced due diligence for any jurisdiction designated as high-risk under FATF public statements. The intraocular lens manufacturing scope (ISIC 3250) is classified as High_Risk_Special_License; therefore, an independent AML/CFT risk assessment, source-of-wealth verification for all UBOs, and ongoing transaction monitoring protocols must be documented prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic portal at www.lbr.lu; name availability pre-check and blocking performed through the LBR 'dénomination' module of the eRegistre platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended, the company name may be expressed in any language, but it must be transcribed in Latin alphabetical characters for registration in the RCS. The notarial deed of incorporation and all RCS filing documents must be prepared in one of the three administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German or Luxembourgish); if the proposed name is drawn from a non-Latin script, a statutory transliteration into Latin characters must be filed and certified by the notary. Where the statutes are drafted in another EU language, the notary typically requires a certified French translation for publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des Sociétés et Associations). The name must be distinguishable from all pre-existing registered names, must not mislead as to the nature or legal form of the company, and must be followed or preceded by the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of the RCS within fifteen (15) working days of the formal rejection notice, setting out the grounds on which the name satisfies uniqueness and public-order conditions under Article 3 of the Law of 10 August 1915. The Registrar must respond within one month. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) pursuant to the RCS procedural rules, requesting annulment of the registrar's decision. A reserved name that expires after 30 days may be re-filed for a new reservation period; however, priority is lost upon expiry and a third party may appropriate the name. In parallel, the applicant may request, through the notary of incorporation, a substitute-name clearance certificate so that the notarial deed execution is not delayed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office with no physical presence is not permissible for a Luxembourg SARL engaged in medical device manufacturing. Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 requires the registered office to be located at a real address in Luxembourg where the corporate records, statutory books and accounting documents are physically kept and where competent authorities may effect service. A domiciliation arrangement with a licensed Luxembourg corporate-services provider is allowed, provided the service provider holds the requisite professional authorization, the domiciliation agreement identifies the company and its managers, and the address is a genuine operational reception address. Nevertheless, for a production company under ISIC 3250 manufacturing intraocular acrylic lenses, the RCS and health inspectorate expect an actual operating manufacturing facility or distribution facility in Luxembourg; reliance solely on a domiciliation address would trigger adverse commercial-substance findings, tax residence challenges, and enhanced AML scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk for this industry: estimated 45-55% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of registration, driven by (i) routine RCS/LBR verification of registered-office existence; (ii) the Direction de la Santé medical-device licensing authority conducting Good Manufacturing Practice audits under EU Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR); (iii) a probable bank due-diligence site visit because the business is classified High_Risk_Special_License with SWIFT and letter-of-credit payment rails; and (iv) potential inspections coordinated with the CSSF and the FIU under Article 5 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended), Articles 710-1 to 710-25 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), together with the Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés (Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, 14 rue Erasme, L-7270 Luxembourg-Hamm, operating the e-RCS electronic filing portal (www.rcsl.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary, followed by the RCSL registration form and the publication of legal notice in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must have a stated share capital of at least EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Each share must have a nominal value of at least EUR 1.00. Cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked bank account in the name of the company or the notary before the deed is signed; the bank confirmation of deposit is annexed to the deed. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor’s report. The capital cannot be reduced below the legal minimum and distributable reserves must be maintained as required by Article 710-2 of the Law of 1915.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders confirm the full payment of the EUR 12,000 stated capital, comprising 12,000 registered units of EUR 1.00 each, subscribed in accordance with the deed of incorporation. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, being the seat and central administration of the company. RESOLVED, that [Full Name] is appointed as General Manager (Gérant), authorised to act alone and to represent the company, with powers governed by Article 710-14 of the Law of 10 August 1915. RESOLVED, that the General Manager is instructed to open a bank account and to complete all RCSL, environmental, and sectoral licensing formalities necessary for start-up.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and legal due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) through the e-RCS portal, with drafting assistance of a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name search in the RCSL index to ensure that the proposed corporate name, including the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL', is distinguishable from existing companies. Verify that the corporate purpose (precision lathe turning of foldable hydrophobic intraocular lenses, ISIC 3250) is lawful and compatible with the regulated profession requirements of the Law of 2 September 2011. Prepare a draft of the articles of association stating the legal form, name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital and manager mandates.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all shareholders and managers
Legal opinion on corporate purpose (if required by the notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name collides with an existing registration, the notary will recommend an alternative name and the new name must be re-checked; no fee is lost if the amendment is made before the deed is executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notarial escrow or a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the future SARL or of the notary and deposit the minimum stated capital of EUR 12,000. The account shall be released only after the RCSL registration is complete. Obtain a bank certificate evidencing the availability and blocking of funds, which will be attached to the notarial deed. For in-kind contributions, obtain the statutory auditor’s valuation report.
required_dossiers: Statutory auditor’s report on in-kind contributions (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate does not meet the notary’s standard, request a corrected certificate with the full corporate name, account number and blocking clause; re-execution of the deed can occur without change of the deed date if the certificate is issued before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the notarial deed before the Luxembourg notary, including the articles of association, the acceptance of their mandate by the manager(s), the founders’ statement on the registered office, and the confirmation that the capital has been subscribed and fully paid. The notary verifies legal capacity, the legality of the purpose, and the absence of grounds for nullity. The deed must be signed by all shareholders or their notarised attorneys-in-fact.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or written consent of the registered office owner
Notarised powers of attorney for representing shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect, a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) is executed before the same notary; if the registered office address is invalid, a new lease or letter of consent must be supplied before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) – e-RCS electronic filing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits electronically to the RCSL the certified copy of the deed, the beneficial owner declaration, the managers’ curriculum vitae, and the registered office details. The RCSL verifies the legality of the incorporation and, upon acceptance, issues the RCS registration number and enters the company in the register. The official notice is published in the RESA, with the publication fee paid via the e-RCS portal.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed and its official copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL raises a query, the notary has a statutory correction window of 8 days to file an amended document; a refusal of registration may be appealed before the Luxembourg administrative court within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (business permit), Administration des contributions directes, Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Administration des douanes et accises (for EORI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 at the Ministry of the Economy, demonstrating the manager’s personal and professional qualifications for the industrial activity. Register with the tax authorities for the national identification number (matricule d'impôt), corporate income tax, net wealth tax and VAT. File the employer registration with the CCSS and obtain an EORI number for the import and export of medical devices and raw materials.
required_dossiers: Description of the manufacturing process and premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business permit is refused, an appeal may be filed with the administrative tribunal within 3 months; if tax or social security data is incomplete, the administration will issue a rectification request and the company must respond within the stated deadline, generally 8 to 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical device, environmental and occupational licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Santé (Direction de la Santé), Administration de l'environnement, Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), municipal building and fire-safety authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the classified-establishment operating permit application to the Administration de l'environnement for the manufacturing facility, including a screening file for the EIA. Register as a legal manufacturer of class III medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) in EUDAMED and notify the Ministry of Health; designate a Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance and an EU Authorised Representative if the manufacturer is not established in the EU. Obtain the fire-safety clearance and occupational workplace inspection before production begins.
required_dossiers: EIA report (if required by screening decision)
EU MDR economic operator registration documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Administration de l'environnement requests corrections, the technical report must be amended and resubmitted within the prescribed time; if the MDR registration is rejected, the Ministry of Health will grant a corrective period, and a subsequent refusal may be challenged before the administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration de l'environnement for the classified-establishment operating permit; Ministère de la Santé (Direction de la Santé) for medical device registration under EU MDR 2017/745; Ministère de l'Économie for the business permit (autorisation d'établissement); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploiter un établissement classé (Classified Establishment Operating Permit) issued under the amended Law of 10 June 1999; cumulative registration as a medical device manufacturer and economic operator in EUDAMED under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, together with the autorisation d'établissement issued under the Law of 2 September 2011 and the ISO 13485 certification for the quality management system.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Environmental Impact Assessment Division (Département de l'évaluation des incidences sur l'environnement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 registered establishment under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 July 2013; an EIA screening is mandatory, while a full EIA report is required only if production or solvent consumption thresholds are exceeded (e.g., solvent consumption above 200 tonnes per year); a small-batch intraocular lens lathe-turning facility will normally be approved with conditions without a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU where applicable; VOC emission limit values and solvent management plan; wastewater discharge limits in accordance with the municipal regulations transposing Directive 91/271/EEC; waste management obligations under the Law of 9 May 2014 on waste, including tracking documents for acrylic swarf and chemical residues; ISO 14644-1 cleanroom particle standards; safe handling and storage of flammable cleaning and sterilisation agents under the Labour Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety conformity certificate issued by the municipal fire service, including structural load inspection of the cleanroom and lathe-turning floors; occupational workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering machine guarding under Directive 2006/42/EC, ventilation, emergency exits, and chemical safety data sheets; occupational medicine programme with a licensed occupational physician before commencement of operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and indirect tax registration; unified online portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet (https://guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity establishing economic activity or a permanent establishment in Luxembourg, the applicant must file the standard business registration form with the AED via MyGuichet, appoint a Luxembourg-resident VAT representative (responsable solidaire) for non-established taxable persons, and annex the notarised articles of incorporation, proof of identity of the legal representative, and documentation evidencing the intended taxable activity (e.g. supply of intraocular acrylic lenses into Luxembourg/EU markets). The AED issues the national matricule and a Luxembourg VAT identification number with the 'LU' prefix; the ACD subsequently assigns the corporate income tax reference upon filing the declaration of commencement of activity. Non-resident companies with no local establishment but making distance sales or imports into Luxembourg must register for VAT through the EU MOSS/non-established person procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. A SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) is mandatorily opaque and is fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICB) and net wealth tax (IChN). No hybrid mismatch election is available to a SARL as such; ATAD-aligned hybrid mismatch rules (Art. 168ter LIR) are applied to neutralise mismatches on cross-border hybrid instruments or payments. The statutory election to be taxed as a corporate entity under Article 6 LIR is available only to fiscally transparent partnerships (SCS/SCSp), not to a SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: The SARL is a resident corporate taxpayer when its registered office or central administration is in Luxembourg; worldwide income is taxable subject to territorial and participation exemption reliefs, and the standard corporate income tax rate is 17% plus the 7% solidarity surcharge (effective aggregate CT rate for 2025: 24.94% in Luxembourg City including municipal business tax).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA) as implemented by the Luxembourg VAT Act (Loi TVA) and harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-enterprise exemption (Art. 57 Loi TVA). Non-established taxable persons supplying goods or services in Luxembourg are subject to mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply, without benefit of the EUR 35,000 threshold. EU-distance-sales thresholds apply as set out in Directive 2006/112/EC (EUR 10,000 cross-border intra-community threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing via the PEPPOL network applies to suppliers providing goods/services to Luxembourg public-sector contracting authorities. No general real-time fiscal clearance, API tax stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime is operational for B2B commercial invoices in Luxembourg as of 2025. Invoices must nonetheless satisfy EU authenticity and integrity verification rules, and must be retained for a minimum of 10 years for VAT audit purposes. The AED retains the right to require XML/e-reporting submissions in the context of specific investigations or for operators in certain regulated sectors.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.supply_chain_note: Supplies of medical devices such as implantable intraocular acrylic lenses are subject to the standard 17% VAT rate in Luxembourg (the 3% reduced rate applies only to certain medical products explicitly listed in Annex IV of the Loi TVA, and implantable lenses are not generally within that reduced-rate list). Intra-community acquisitions and cross-border B2B transactions are subject to the reverse-charge mechanism when zero-rated or place-of-supply rules relocate the burden.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: the 0% export rate is available for intraocular acrylic lenses physically transported outside the European Union within 3 months of supply, provided the exporter holds the customs SAD EXIT confirmation and appropriate transport evidence. Intra-Community dispatches to a customer with a valid EU VAT identification number are zero-rated provided the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) is filed. Services: 0% or reverse charge applies to cross-border B2B services where the place of supply is outside Luxembourg under Article 14 of the Loi TVA (e.g. contract manufacturing, toll conversion, logistical services, licensing of lens-related IP), evidenced by commercial contracts, proof of recipient's business status, and financial flows. All export zero-rating claims must be documented in a complete 'export file' kept at the disposal of the AED for a minimum of 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD form, Export/EX item with EXIT confirmation from the Luxembourg or EU customs system)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice and purchase order (or pro forma invoice) describing the intraocular acrylic lenses, quantity, value and HS/SAD classification
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer/payment proof evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax practice subjects export zero-rating claims to strict documentary review by the AED. Missing, contradictory or falsified customs/transport evidence triggers retrospective VAT clawback (the standard-rate VAT becomes due at the time of supply), default interest accruing from the original due date, and administrative penalties of up to twice the VAT evaded. Fraudulent use of forged customs stamps or false export declarations constitutes criminal tax evasion (escroquerie en matière de TVA) punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and/or criminal fines up to EUR 25,000, in addition to complete exclusion of the taxpayer from future zero-rating schemes and debarment from customs simplified procedures. Companies failing the 180-day inward remittance substantiation may also face transfer pricing adjustments and corporate income tax penalties for unrepatriated export revenue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with prudential supervision exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); Luxembourg's exchange-control powers operate within the EU Treaty framework (Article 63 TFEU, free movement of capital) and the Luxembourg AML/CTF law of 12 November 2004.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc is fully superseded by the euro; foreign-exchange controls are abolished. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible and unrestricted, with no requirement for central-bank approval for cross-border transfers. The only obligations are statistical: balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL, EMIR trade reporting for derivatives, and CRS/FATCA transparency. Profit remittance is frictionless from an FX standpoint; the sole domestic structural cost is a 15% withholding tax on dividends, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% qualifying holding for 12 months) or under an applicable double-tax treaty. No Luxembourg withholding tax applies to royalties paid to non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. Luxembourg imposes no statutory requirement for surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds. Export receipts in USD, CHF, CNY, or other convertible currencies may be retained freely in any jurisdiction. Compliance is limited to: (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border transactions above the applicable reporting threshold; (ii) VAT/intrastat filing obligations for intra-EU dispatches; and (iii) documentation of the underlying trade transaction where payment flows exceed €10,000, as required by CSSF AML circulars.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR/USD Account
Operational Account plus Trade Finance (Documentary Credits and Collections) Facility
Capital Escrow Account, Operational Account, and Commercial Letter-of-Credit Outward Facility
Operational USD Clearing Account with SWIFT MT103/MT202 Cash Management and Treasury Desk
Operational Account with Receivables Discounting and Import/Export Clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate. Luxembourg fintechs holding a CSSF payment-institution (PI) or e-money institution (EMI) licence under PSD2 (Law of 10 November 2009) may provide current-account-style holding, issuance, and SEPA/EUR clearing only. They cannot execute USD correspondent clearing, documentary letters of credit, or ISDA derivatives, and are therefore suitable only for small-value auxiliary treasury buckets. Offshore (non-EU) digital EMIs are not viable: PSD2 passporting does not permit payment services into Luxembourg without a local licence or a registered agent arrangement, and mainstream Luxembourg banks will not accept first-tier account relationships with a high-risk medical-device manufacturer channelled through an unlicensed offshore EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the normative requirement. Under the Luxembourg AML law and CSSF Regulation 12-01, the banking responsible officer (RL) must identify the legal representatives, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) before account opening. For a high-risk special-licence manufacturing entity, banks will require at least one director or the primary UBO to appear in person in Luxembourg, or before a Luxembourg notary granting a power of attorney. Remote video-KYC via LuxTrust or eIDAS-certified channels may supplement but rarely replace the face-to-face interview for the opening account; banks in the same EU group may accept a physical interview at a sister branch in France or Germany, but this is discretionary and must be pre-agreed in writing. Non-EU resident directors are almost always required to attend personally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the LU_SARL's ultimate shareholders are layered through multiple Luxembourg SCS/SCSp vehicles or non-EU discretionary trusts, making beneficial ownership unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified statuts and current RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) extract; up-to-date register of beneficial owners (Modèle B) filed in the e-RCS; shareholding chain diagram descending to natural persons; passport copies of each UBO; notarised source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; independent bank references; audit-confirmed proof of subscribed capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High_Risk_Special_License flag: intraocular acrylic lens manufacturing is classified by the bank as high-risk, and the compliance team questions the validity of the statutory manufacturing licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licence to manufacture medical devices issued by the Direction de la Santé / Ministry of Health; CE certificates under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) issued by a notified body; ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certificate; designation document for the European authorised representative; product classification sheet; annual LNS (Laboratoire National de Santé) export certificate for each shipment batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP name-match alert: a foreign director, UBO, or correspondent beneficiary produces a positive screening hit against EU/US sanction lists or a PEP database.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Re-run name-screening clearance report; CVs and proof of residence of all directors/UBOs; PEP-status declaration or absence-of-PEP statement; notarised sworn declaration as to origin of wealth; apostilled police clearance certificates from the country of residence; notarised power of attorney where personal attendance is impossible; screening-analyst write-off memorandum with legal basis for non-matching genuine economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch: proposed USD inflows from ophthalmic distributors and hospital tenders are inconsistent with the SARL's declared head-office costs and manufacturing footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master supply and distribution agreements; purchase orders; proforma and final commercial invoices; airway bills and bills of lading; CMR consignment notes; customs export declarations filed with the Administration des douanes et accises; bank MT103 evidence trail matching invoice values; audited statutory financial statements for the SARL; transfer-pricing file proving arm's-length allocation of manufacturing versus head-office functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering concern: the bank flags imports of acrylate/polymer lens components from high-risk or unusual customs corridors (e.g., offshore free zones or CIS rail routes).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full supplier KYC pack containing GMP/ISO certificates and compliance declarations; itemised bill of materials; country-of-origin certificates; purchase-order chronology; end-to-end logistics contracts; customs entry records with HS 9001.30 tariff classification; independent third-party customs-broker report; insurance declarations whose insured values reconcile with payment flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the LU_SARL's paid-in capital injection (minimum subscribed capital €12,000 under the Law of 23 June 2016, fully paid and deposited with the bank), the compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 credit in EUR (or SEPA Credit Transfer where the parent is EU-domiciled). The purpose code must follow the BCL balance-of-payments taxonomy generically as 'C00 / Equity Capital Investment — Capital Contribution — Share Subscription'; the reference line must state 'LU_SARL CAPITAL INCREASE / SHARE PREMIUM / ESCROW — [NOTARY DEED REF].' The bank will require: the notarial or private deed of capital increase; resolution of the shareholders' meeting; proof of identity of the remitter and the UBOs; confirmation that funds originate from a regulated banking institution; and, where the injection exceeds large-transaction thresholds, an automated BCL statistical report and an internal source-of-funds statement. Proceeds must remain segregated in a capital escrow account until the RCS filing is completed and the register of beneficial owners is updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound trade settlement must be channelled through the relationship bank's cash-management and documentary trade desks. Standard rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for EUR and USD wires, with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for domestic/EU payments; (ii) commercial letters of credit, both sight and usance, issued/advised through the bank's trade module and confirmed by a top-tier EU or US correspondent bank for non-EU buyers; (iii) standby letters of credit and tender guarantees for hospital procurement contracts; (iv) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for recurring distributor orders; (v) supply-chain finance and reverse factoring for inbound component purchases; (vi) USD settlement via the bank's New York correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire) and CNY settlement via CIPS where applicable. Each disbursement must carry the underlying contract and import/export customs references and be supported by invoice, packing list, and transport documents for amounts above €50,000; BCL balance-of-payments coding must distinguish 'trade settlement' from 'intercompany financing' to avoid recharacterisation risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts (tenors up to 24 months) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Luxembourg, French, or German EU-authorised bank; EMIR reporting to a registered trade repository is mandatory.
EUR/USD FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) used exclusively for rolling export-receipt liquidity without creating a speculative open position.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS/CCIRS) converting USD working-capital or LC-financed drawings into EUR floating-rate funding, subject to ISDA CSA collateral arrangements.
European-style OTC currency options for protection on non-binding public hospital tender prices in third-country currencies; premiums must be economically justifiable and not speculative.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible Asian/CIS invoicing currencies (e.g., INR, VND, NGN) where the underlying exposure is a genuine intraocular-lens export receivable; permitted only through an EU/EEA-authorized dealer and documented under IFRS 9 hedge accounting.
Synthetic forward rollovers embedded in bank treasury lines, limited to the SARL's verified quarterly net exposure, with all transactions benchmarked against EURIBOR/€STR where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) of shareholders - approval of annual accounts, discharge of managers and reappointment of the statutory auditor where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; minutes and attendance sheets retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office in Luxembourg; no government filing occurs at the AGM stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end, i.e. by 30 June for a 31 December year-end; the first AGM must be held within 18 months of incorporation; the commercial court may extend the deadline on justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On persistent failure to hold the AGM, the commercial court may, at the request of any interested party and after a 3-month summons, order judicial dissolution under Article 14 of the Law of 10 August 1915; delinquent managers additionally bear civil liability to shareholders for consequential loss

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts deposit - balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes, management report and, if audit is mandatory, the independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), Ministry of Justice; mandatory electronic filing via the single LBR platform (lbr.lu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date, i.e. by 31 July for a 31 December year-end; approval by the AGM normally occurs on 30 June and the deposit must be filed within one month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default fines progressively accrued by the RCS custodian up to EUR 5,000 pursuant to Article 14 of the Law of 10 August 1915; judicial summons and publication of the failure at the company's expense; unresolved default for 3 months authorizes the commercial court to order administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (IRC) return, combined with municipal business tax (IS) and net wealth tax (IFT) declaration on Form 1001
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; national electronic e-filing portal for corporate returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the tax year for paper filing; automatic extension to 30 June for electronic filing; the ACD may, upon request, extend the deadline to 31 December of the filing year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to EUR 6,000 plus a 10% increase for deliberate concealment; automatic late-payment interest at 2.4% per annum under the 2025 rate scale, accruing from six months after the tax year-end; provisional assessment and enforced recovery proceedings if the return remains outstanding

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax (impot minimum sur la fortune) payment for the SARL - annual minimum NWT liability of EUR 3,500, reduced from EUR 10,000 under the 2025 Finance Law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Net Wealth Tax service; payment by direct debit or ACD bank transfer and reported on Form 1001
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Single instalment due by 30 June of the fiscal year for a calendar-year taxpayer; the NWT charge crystallizes on 1 January of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 2.4% per annum under the 2025 scale; enforced recovery by ACD seizure; the minimum NWT remains due irrespective of loss-making years and constitutes the mandatory annual floor for an active SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO data filing and confirmation - declaration of beneficial owners of the SARL, being any individual owning or controlling more than 25% of the entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre des beneficiaires effectifs (RBE), Ministry of Justice; electronic application via lbr.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 15 days of incorporation; declaration of any shareholding transfer or control change within 15 days of the event; annual reconciliation of the RBE dataset completed and certified at the AGM date (30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and criminal fines for non-filing and for inaccurate data, with per-entity administrative sanctions up to EUR 1,250 and criminal fines applicable to managers; subsequent non-compliance blocks bank financing and, on continued default, triggers RCS enforcement and possible strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit - verification of the share register, pledge register, option register and minutes book against the share transfer ledger
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; registers maintained on site at the registered office and made available to members, notaries, banks and the RCS upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the AGM (30 June); registers must reflect the shareholding structure as at the balance-sheet date (31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Luxembourg commercial code, a share transfer not recorded in the statutory share register is ineffective against third parties; managing partners are liable for rectification of a defective register and shareholders may obtain a court order compelling the update

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit by a Luxembourg-approved statutory auditor (reviseur d'entreprises agree) is compulsory when the SARL exceeds any two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce exceeding 50 employees; audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, regulated financial institutions, securitization vehicles, parent undertakings preparing consolidated accounts, and upon the application of shareholders holding one-tenth of the subscribed capital
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as enacted by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register, applying the standardized formats of the Luxembourg normalised chart of accounts for a commercial undertaking; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for the unconsolidated annual accounts and is required for the consolidated accounts of listed parent undertakings; a medical-device manufacturing SARL files under the ordinary commercial annual-accounts format

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers and any change to the beneficial-ownership dataset must be declared to the RBE within 15 days of the event; at each year-end the company's compliance officer reconciles the members' ledger against transfer documentation, audits the share register, files any resulting corrections with the RBE and certifies the annual confirmation in the AGM minutes; deliberate false declarations expose the SARL and its managers to fines and publication sanctions, and an accurate RBE registration remains a precondition for profit distributions and for recognition of the entity by EU counterparties and financing institutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500 - US$4,000 per annum (Luxembourg-City domiciliation and registered-office service with corporate-secretarial support, AGM logistics and annual register updating; medium range for a manufacturing SARL without a physical establishment)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$9,000 - US$28,000 per annum (Luxembourg-approved statutory audit by a reviseur d'entreprises agree for a mid-sized industrial entity, depending on turnover, stock valuation, and intra-group transaction volume)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined corporate income tax (CIT) statutory headline rate in Luxembourg City (2025): CIT 17.00% + solidarity/unemployment fund surcharge 7% of CIT = 1.19% + municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) 6.75%; lower bracket of 15% applies to the first €175,000 of taxable base, with a 31.5% marginal phase-out band between €175,001 and €200,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: i. Participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR): 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains (≥10% holding or ≥€1.2M acquisition cost; ≥12-month holding; subject-to-tax condition). ii. IP Box (Art. 50bis LIR): 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income (e.g., patented manufacturing processes, software copyrights) → effective combined rate ≈ 4.98%. iii. R&D super-deduction: 20% additional deduction (Law of 17 July 2015, as amended) on qualifying R&D expenses. iv. No capital gains tax on shares held ≥6 months (grandfathering for tax-resident individuals only — not relevant for SARL); employee stock-option regime does not apply to lens manufacturer. Note: manufacturing operations benefit from no customs preference; normal depreciation (declining balance up to 30%) applies
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit under LIR Art. 169; carry-back is prohibited; losses may offset 100% of future taxable income; nil-year ring-fencing applies to municipal business tax and CIT alike)
